subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Should ClawHub adopt a v1 advisory routing-and-verification metadata contract, and if so which fields and consumers are stable enough to support before ranking or policy behavior is added?
rationale: The proposal introduces new registry semantics across skills, plugins, API/CLI consumers, and security communication; source inspection cannot determine the intended durable contract or authority boundary.

options.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
options.body: Standardize optional intents, exclusions, and human-readable verification hints with raw API/CLI exposure, while keeping risk data non-authoritative and deferring ranking.

options.title: Design the full trust model first
options.body: Defer implementation until maintainers define validation, keyword-abuse handling, and how advisory declarations interact with scanner and moderation evidence.

options.title: Keep this external to ClawHub
options.body: Leave routing indexes and evaluation policy to Harness implementations and retain only existing install, compatibility, and scan metadata in the registry.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
recommendation.body: Standardize optional intents, exclusions, and human-readable verification hints with raw API/CLI exposure, while keeping risk data non-authoritative and deferring ranking.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged implementation establishes the schema/parser extension pattern that any chosen v1 would build on.
